build_inputs.angles:
That sound you just heard gets compared to a vacuum cleaner. It is a Porsche 911, and it gets to sixty in four point three seconds.

This is the 992 Carrera T. A three litre twin turbo flat six, three hundred and seventy nine horsepower, and a seven speed manual as standard, which almost nothing else at this money still gives you.

Here is the strange part. Porsche built the T by taking things away. The rear seats are gone. The glass is thinner. There is less sound deadening. It weighs about a hundred pounds less than a normal Carrera.

And it is not faster. The automatic Carrera beats it to sixty by half a second. You are paying Porsche money for the slower car.

What you get back is the shifter, the lighter nose, and that noise. Some people think that is worth every cent.

script: It hits sixty in four point three seconds, but you paid extra to lose a hundred pounds and keep the same 379 horsepower. The 992 Porsche 911 Carrera T takes its name from the 911 T that gave Porsche its first Monte Carlo Rally win in 1968. Porsche made the sport suspension standard here and set it ten millimeters lower than the base Carrera. The diet starts with thinner glass and less sound deadening, and Porsche leaves the rear seats out unless you ask. It also borrows the limited-slip differential from the S. The three-liter twin-turbo flat-six makes 331 pound-feet of torque, just like the base Carrera, and it’ll rev to seventy-five hundred. The seven-speed stick comes standard, but the automatic Porsche 911 Carrera with Sport Chrono gets to sixty half a second sooner. They started around $120,000 new, and they go for about $130,000 today. Would you pay for less?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2023 Porsche 911 Carrera T Coupe, finished in GT Silver Metallic with a black interior, and will be displayed live at Willow Springs Reimagined as part of the Cars & Bids Willow Springs Collection. This 911 features the desirable 7-speed manual transmission. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this 911 is a Carrera T model, and comes equipped with over $13,000 in options. A partial list of notable equipment includes the Sport Chrono Package, 20-inch wheels in Satin Black, Porsche Active Suspension Management (PASM), a front axle lift system, a sports exhaust system, 18-way Adaptive Sport Seats Plus, and a Surround View camera. Notable modifications reported by the seller include clear side marker lights, Kies Motorsports wheel spacers, a Nine Volt MagSafe phone charger, and a NOCO quick connect battery charger. Released for 2023, the 992 Carrera T borrows several performance features from the Carrera S, including a standard mechanical limited-slip differential, lowered PASM sport suspension, and a sports exhaust system – and it sheds 100 pounds compared to the base Carrera, thanks to several weight-saving measures, like reduced deadening and thinner window glass. Power comes from a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter flat-6, rated at 379 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed manual transmission.
